findings.explanation: The new GET /users/<int:user_id>/orders endpoint only applies @require_auth and then returns all orders where Order.user_id == user_id. It never calls is_owner_or_admin(g.current_user, user_id), so any authenticated user can list any other user's orders. This directly violates security-policy.md §3 ('Listing another user's orders is restricted to that user themselves and administrators') and api-spec.md which lists '/users/<id>/orders GET — owner or admin'. The sibling endpoints in the same file (get_user, update_user) correctly enforce is_owner_or_admin, confirming the intended pattern.

evidence.content: Listing another user's orders is restricted to that user themselves and administrators.

findings.suggested_fix:
Add an ownership check before returning data, e.g.:

    if not is_owner_or_admin(g.current_user, user_id):
        return jsonify({"error": "forbidden"}), 403

immediately after the @require_auth decorator (mirroring get_user/update_user in the same file).
